chunks: Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, charity and alms-tax are not given preferentially to the near (kin), nor are they prevented from the remote (non-kin).

key_terms.يُحَابَى: To show favoritism or give preferential treatment

ai.seo_question: Does being a relative give one priority in receiving Zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies that while kinship is respected, it does not create an exclusive legal right to Zakat, ensuring distribution remains based on merit and need. This principle is central to Shia jurisprudence, particularly in distinguishing between the general public and the specific recipients of Wilayah, preventing nepotism in charitable distribution. It underscores the impartiality of divine commandments regarding wealth purification.

en.hubeali:
Hammad Bin Isa, from hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The charity and the Zakāt, cannot be gifted to the near ones, and would not be prevented to the remote ones’.
en.sarwar: 3. Hammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Zakat cannot be given as a gift to relatives or be denied to non-relatives.’”
